question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{2{x}^{2}+6x}$ at the point where $x=3$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=2{x}^{2}+6x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x+6.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (4x+6) \\  & =\frac{2(2x+3)}{2\sqrt{2{x}^{2}+6x}} \\  & =\frac{2x+3}{\sqrt{2{x}^{2}+6x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=3} & ={(\frac{2x+3}{\sqrt{2{x}^{2}+6x}})|}_{x=3} \\  & =\frac{4(3)+6}{2\sqrt{2(3{)}^{2}+6(3)}} \\  & =\frac{18}{2\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{4{x}^{2}-7x}$ at the point where $x=4$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=4{x}^{2}-7x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=8x-7.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (8x-7) \\  & =\frac{8x-7}{2\sqrt{4{x}^{2}-7x}} \\  & =\frac{8x-7}{2\sqrt{4{x}^{2}-7x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=4} & ={(\frac{8x-7}{2\sqrt{4{x}^{2}-7x}})|}_{x=4} \\  & =\frac{8(4)-7}{2\sqrt{4(4{)}^{2}-7(4)}} \\  & =\frac{25}{2\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{25}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-5{x}^{2}+9x}$ at the point where $x=1$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-5{x}^{2}+9x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=9-10x.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (9-10x) \\  & =-\frac{10x-9}{2\sqrt{-5{x}^{2}+9x}} \\  & =-\frac{10x-9}{2\sqrt{-5{x}^{2}+9x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(-\frac{10x-9}{2\sqrt{-5{x}^{2}+9x}})|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{9-10(1)}{2\sqrt{-5(1{)}^{2}+9(1)}} \\  & =\frac{-1}{2\sqrt{4}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{37+7x}$ at the point where $x=-4.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=37+7x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=7.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (7) \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{37+7x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-4,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-4} & ={(\frac{7}{2\sqrt{37+7x}})|}_{x=-4} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{37+7(-4)}} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{7}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{-7x+16}$ at the point where $x=0$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=-7x+16.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-7.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot -7 \\  & =-\frac{7}{2\sqrt{-7x+16}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=0} & ={(-\frac{7}{2\sqrt{-7x+16}})|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{-7}{2\sqrt{-7(0)+16}} \\  & =\frac{-7}{2\sqrt{16}} \\  & =-\frac{7}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
